% Extended Data Fig. 1 (horizon), as placed in Overleaf extended_data.tex; generated by horizon_study/make_ed_horizon_nature.py
\begin{figure}[p]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.8\linewidth]{Figures/ed_horizon.pdf}
\caption{\textbf{Post-cutoff performance by forecast horizon.}
Horizon is the number of months from the knowledge cutoff of a model to the first public observation of an event.
Post-cutoff events (horizon of one month or more) of the full corpus (January 2024 to August 2026), nine models of Table~\ref{tab:main_results}, base condition.
Points are the means of the bins 1--3, 4--6, 7--12, 13--24 and more than 24 months (alternate bins shaded), at the mean horizon of each bin; marker area shows the number of items.
Ribbons are 95\% event-level bootstrap confidence intervals (10,000 samples); bins with fewer than 20 items are not shown.
\textbf{a}, Balanced accuracy (mean of the accuracies on original and perturbed questions).
\textbf{b}, Yes/no bias (accuracy on original minus perturbed questions; positive means too many yes answers).
\textbf{c}, \textbf{e}, Mean stated confidence.
\textbf{d}, MCQ accuracy.
\textbf{f}, FRQ rubric score.
\textbf{g}, \textbf{h}, Absolute and signed error of the predicted month (positive means later than the true month).
Dashed lines: chance (\textbf{a}, \textbf{d}), no bias (\textbf{b}), no error (\textbf{h}), pass threshold (\textbf{f}).
In a mixed model with random intercepts for event and model, MCQ accuracy decreases by 0.17 log-odds per year of horizon (95\% CI 0.05 to 0.29; Holm $p=0.06$).
Balanced accuracy stays close to chance, but the yes/no bias increases: $+$0.74 log-odds per year on original questions and $-$0.66 on perturbed questions.
Stated confidence changes by at most 0.03 (MCQ) and 0.08 (Binary) across the bins of each model.
In every bin, MCQ confidence is 0.16--0.40 above the accuracy for GPT-4o, LLaMA~3.3, GPT-OSS and DeepSeek R1, and 0.26--0.41 below it for Claude Opus~4.8 and Claude Sonnet~5.
Thus, the models do not express more uncertainty about events further beyond their cutoff.
The FRQ score does not change ($+$0.01 points per year, 95\% CI $-$0.01 to $+$0.04).
The decrease of the date error mostly comes from anchoring (\textbf{h}): for the six models with a horizon range of at least 7 months, a constant prediction at the median predicted month of each model gives a decrease of the same size or larger (Supplementary Section~\ref{sec:si_horizon}).}
\label{fig:ed_horizon}
\end{figure}
